messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — I think we need a concise statement of ownership for each surface between Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Current doc is fuzzy on secrets, tracing, and rollout policy.
aj: 100% — can we list the hot spots and then say "owner: control-plane" or "owner: runtime"? keeps handoffs explicit.
kevin: +1. My concern: rollback/fallback semantics when runtime can't honor a policy (e.g., KMS not reachable). need policy for fail-open vs fail-closed.
lucy: For Private we already agreed to default to fail-closed for key material, but for Hosted we favor fail-open with audit. worth documenting separately.
maria: proposed minimal model: each capability gets (1) primary owner, (2) guaranteed contract, (3) graceful-degradation options. examples: auth tokens, kms unwrap, telemetry, model-variant selection, batching config.
aj: That sounds actionable. can we propose a tiny RPC surface as the contract between control-plane and runtime? something minimal so adapters can be thin.
kevin: sketch:
```
// control -> runtime
CheckCapacity(tenant, model, seqLen) -> {ok, reason}
DispatchRequest(req) -> {stream|error}
InvalidateCache(prefix)
ReportTelemetry(batch)
// runtime -> control
NotifyEviction(tenant, reason)
HandshakeCapabilities() -> [capabilities]
```
lucy: I like it. add a Capability enum so runtime advertises e.g. [KMS_DELEGATION, KV_CACHE, STREAMING, QUANTIZED_INFER]. then control-plane can decide routing.
infra-bot: noted: add telemetry schema change to infra-telemetry backlog #T-4321 :memo:
maria: two tricky policy areas we must call out explicitly: (A) secrets management (who must have keys in private deployments vs hosted), (B) rollout/trial feature gating (who can force fallback to smaller model).
aj: For (A) propose: Hosted => control-plane can unwrap on behalf of runtime (audited). Dedicated => optional customer KMS plugin, default same as hosted unless customer provides a key. Private => runtime-managed keys; control-plane only stores references.
kevin: For (B) propose: control-plane owns rollout config, runtime must support a defined canary header. If runtime cannot perform fine-grained canary, control-plane must do coarse routing and mark the runtime capability as limited.
lucy: edge-case: offline private runtime (no control-plane). need a local policy file that mirrors rollout decisions with TTL. otherwise features break.
maria: yes — define sync contract: control-plane publishes signed policy blobs with ttl. runtime verifies sig and applies when offline.
aj: example blob shape:
```
{ "issued_by": "control", "zid": "acct123", "rollouts": [{"route":"/chat","model":"m-p-3","pct":5}], "exp": 1680000000, "sig": "..." }
```
kevin: question: observability — who owns traces/span naming? If both do, dashboards get noisy. propose naming prefix: control-plane spans use cp.*, runtime spans use rt.* and we join by request_id.
lucy: Also need to decide where token-level billing attribution happens. we decided earlier control-plane one source of truth — confirm in this thread.
maria: confirm: billing attribution in control-plane; runtime reports per-request tokens and request_id back. control-plane aggregates.
infra-bot: FYI: quota-service changes required for attribute propagation. ticket #Q-778 created.
deploy-bot: deploy check: API change to rpc.HandshakeCapabilities() needs schema bump v1.2. Deploy window suggested 03/24 09:00-11:00 UTC.
aj: Action items: (1) I'll draft a short owner matrix table mapping capabilities -> owner/contract/degradation. (2) @kevin will draft signed-policy blob spec. (3) @lucy will write trace/span naming convention. (4) @maria will update RFC text with these additions.
kevin: one more: fallback ordering: try same-host runtime variants -> region fallback -> hosted fallback. document as list and include SLA implications.
lucy: ping on compatibility: we should allow older runtime versions to advertise a subset of capabilities and control-plane should treat missing capabilities as "limited" not error.
maria: agree. we'll include a migration plan: stage 1 advertise-only, stage 2 enforce routing decisions, stage 3 deprecate old behaviour after N days.
aj: cool. i'll post the matrix by EOD. anyone object to me owning the PR?
kevin: no objections.
maria: thanks. small ask: when you post the matrix, include explicit examples for KMS unavailability and an offline private runtime scenario. makes reviews quicker.
lucy: noted.
maria: ok closing for now. will link updated RFC when PR lands. :white_check_mark:
